purpose: Close the source-normalized loophole left by v1.2. Tovey bounded-occurrence normalization needs degree-3 equality variables and OR2/OR3 clauses, but no EQ4. This theorem proves that EQ3+OR2+OR3 already cannot share one common holographic basis that makes all three matchgate signatures.

setup.basis: Let S be invertible and T=S^(-T). Variable tensors transform by S, clause tensors by T.
setup.necessary_condition: Every matchgate signature obeys parity: its support is contained entirely in even Hamming weight or entirely in odd Hamming weight. For arity 2 and 3 this necessary condition is enough for the present impossibility proof; no stronger matchgate identity is assumed.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_BASIS_FOR_EQ3_OR2_OR3_MATCHGATE_PARITY
theorem.statement: Over characteristic zero, there is no invertible 2x2 matrix S such that S^tensor3 EQ3, T^tensor2 OR2, and T^tensor3 OR3 all satisfy matchgate parity, where T=S^(-T).
proof: Put q=T e0=(q0,q1) and p=T(e0+e1)=(p0,p1). Since T is invertible, p and q are independent. The transformed OR_k is p^tensork-q^tensork.

If transformed OR2 is even-parity, p0*p1=q0*q1. If this product is nonzero, combining with either parity choice for OR3 forces p=q after taking ratios. If it is zero, independence forces p and q onto opposite coordinate axes, so OR3 has nonzero weight-0 and weight-3 entries and violates parity. Therefore OR2 cannot be even-parity.
Hence OR2 is odd-parity: p0^2=q0^2 and p1^2=q1^2. Independence implies q0,q1 are nonzero and p0=epsilon0*q0, p1=epsilon1*q1 with epsilon0,epsilon1 in {+1,-1} and epsilon0 != epsilon1.

If OR3 is even-parity, its weight-1 and weight-3 equations force epsilon1=+1, hence epsilon0=-1. Thus p=(-q0,q1). Since the columns of T are q and p-q, T=[[q0,-2q0],[q1,0]]. Therefore S=T^(-T)=[[0,-1/(2q0)],[1/q1,1/(2q1)]]. Writing its columns as u,v, the transformed EQ3=u^tensor3+v^tensor3 has weight-0 coefficient v0^3 !=0 and weight-1 coefficient v0^2*v1 !=0. It has both parities, contradiction.

If OR3 is odd-parity, its weight-0 and weight-2 equations force epsilon0=+1, hence epsilon1=-1. Thus p=(q0,-q1), T=[[q0,0],[q1,-2q1]], and S=[[1/q0,1/(2q0)],[0,-1/(2q1)]]. Again transformed EQ3 has a nonzero weight-0 coefficient and a nonzero weight-1 coefficient, contradiction.

source_alignment.Tovey_fact: The standard bounded-occurrence reduction replaces repeated variables by copies and adds cyclic 2-clauses enforcing equality. Every copy occurs once in an original clause and twice in the implication cycle, so the natural tensor vocabulary is exactly EQ3 together with OR2 and OR3.
source_alignment.consequence: Removing EQ4 from the old v1.2 test does not reopen the one-common-basis matchgate route.

killed: One common invertible 2x2 holographic basis for all EQ3 variables and OR2/OR3 clauses followed by local matchgate conversion.
not_killed: Nonlocal Pfaffian or determinant cancellation not factored into local common-basis matchgates.
